page: Microsoft Azure HB368-240rs_v5 is a high-performance computing instance built on an x86_64 Intel processor architecture and provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 240 dedicated vCPUs alongside 448.0 GB of system memory, establishing an allocation ratio of approximately 1.87 GB of RAM per core. This architecture focuses compute capacity on parallel execution environments where high core availability takes precedence over massive per-thread memory pools.

Storage and network interfaces are engineered for demanding data throughput. The instance integrates 15,874 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Azure Premium Storage for external managed disks. Network capabilities include RDMA support to enable low-latency communication across multi-node clusters. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on private networking structures typical of clustered environments.

The balance of 240 dedicated compute cores, low per-core memory capacity, and expansive local NVMe storage creates a profile geared toward computational workloads with significant scratch-disk requirements. Tradeoffs include limited memory capacity for memory-bound applications and the absence of hardware accelerators. Appropriate workload fits include tightly coupled high-performance computing, computational fluid dynamics, finite element modeling, molecular dynamics, and large-scale parallel batch processing tasks.
